title: Count Beautiful Substrings I
summary: Given a string s and a positive integer k, count the number of non-empty substrings where the number of vowels equals the number of consonants, and their product is divisible by k.
statement: Given a string s and a positive integer k, count the number of non-empty substrings where the number of vowels equals the number of consonants, and their product is divisible by k. Vowels are 'a', 'e', 'i', 'o', 'u', and consonants are the remaining letters.
constraints: s is a nonempty lowercase string and k is positive.
A substring is beautiful when vowel and consonant counts are equal and their product is divisible by k.
Count all nonempty contiguous beautiful substrings.
hints: Only running vowel and consonant counts are needed for a fixed start.
Enumerate each start and extend right while updating the vowel count in constant time.
Derive consonants from length and test equality plus product modulo k.
Every substring has one unique start/end pair, so the nested scan tests each exactly once with exact counts.
editorial: Every substring has one unique start/end pair, so the nested scan tests each exactly once with exact counts.

tests.explanation: The substrings baey and aeyh each contain two vowels and two consonants, with product four divisible by two.
The substrings ab, ba, and abba are balanced and automatically divisible by one.
